definitions.gloss: external; outward; pertaining to outward appearance
definitions.explanation: Relating to the outward appearance or external look of something, as opposed to its internal substance, function, or character. Used when discussing how something appears on the surface.

examples.japanese: {外観的|がいかんてき}には{問題|もんだい}なさそうだ。
examples.english: It seems to have no problems in terms of outward appearance.

examples.japanese: {外観的|がいかんてき}な{美|うつく}しさだけでなく、{機能性|きのうせい}も{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: Not just external beauty, but functionality is also important.

examples.japanese: この{二|ふた}つの{製品|せいひん}は{外観的|がいかんてき}にはほとんど{同|おな}じだが、{内部|ないぶ}の{構造|こうぞう}は{大|おお}きく{異|こと}なる。
examples.english: These two products look almost the same on the outside, but their internal structures differ greatly.

notes:
Composed of {外観|がいかん} (outward appearance, exterior) and the suffix ～{的|てき} (pertaining to, -like). Used in both everyday and technical contexts to distinguish surface-level characteristics from deeper qualities.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {外観的|がいかんてき}な{特徴|とくちょう}: outward characteristics
- {外観的|がいかんてき}な{変化|へんか}: change in outward appearance
- {外観的|がいかんてき}に{判断|はんだん}する: to judge by outward appearance

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {表面的|ひょうめんてき}: superficial — emphasizes surface-level quality, often with a negative nuance of being shallow
- {見|み}た{目|め}: appearance, looks — a more colloquial way to refer to how something looks
- {内面的|ないめんてき}: internal, inner — the opposite, referring to inner qualities or character
